text: Let's meet the players you'll be comparing throughout this course. Five families of SQL dialect, each with its own name, its own history, and its own personality.

The four traditional relational platforms: SQL Server speaks T-SQL, which you already know. Oracle speaks PL/SQL. MySQL has its own dialect from scratch, shared almost entirely with MariaDB. And PostgreSQL has its own SQL dialect plus a procedural language called PL slash pgSQL.

Here's the same idea, create a stored procedure, in all four. Notice these aren't minor spelling differences -- they're four genuinely different languages for doing anything beyond a single query. Full syntax for each is coming in chapters five and six.

And then there's a fifth family: cloud data warehouses. Snowflake has its own dialect with strong support for semi-structured data. Databricks runs Spark SQL. BigQuery is Google's warehouse with its own functions. And Redshift was actually forked from PostgreSQL, which is why its dialect leans noticeably Postgres-flavored.

These five families are built for analytics at scale, not the transactional workloads the traditional platforms handle. Next lesson, we'll get hands-on: setting up a free practice environment so you can actually run code against most of these platforms yourself.
